exercises.name: Plate-Loaded Donkey Calf Raise
aliases: Elevación de Pantorrilla a la Burra en Máquina
exercises.instructions:
Load the plate horns and step onto the platform with the balls of your feet on the edge and your heels hanging free.
Bend forward at the hips and settle the pad across your hips, then rest your forearms on the support in front of you.
Keep your knees straight and your back flat, with your torso close to parallel to the floor.
Push through the balls of your feet and raise your heels as high as you can, pausing briefly at the top.
Lower your heels below the platform until you feel a strong calf stretch, and repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
cues: The forward hinge is the exercise. Standing up straight turns this into an ordinary standing calf raise and gives away the extra stretch you came for.
Keep the knees straight throughout. Bending them shifts the work from the gastrocnemius to the soleus, which is the seated calf raise, not this one.
Let the heels drop all the way below the platform edge. The bottom of the range is where this machine earns its place, and cutting it short wastes the setup.
exercises.author: RepDB / Sergei Argutin
exercises.attribution: Exercise data and illustrations by RepDB (https://repdb.co/exercise/plate-loaded-donkey-calf-raise/), RepDB Free Tier 1.0 (https://github.com/RepDB/exercise-dataset/blob/main/LICENSE-DATA.md).

exercises.name: Plate-Loaded Glute Drive
aliases: Empuje de Glúteo en Máquina de Discos
exercises.instructions:
Load the plate horns evenly and sit into the machine with your upper back against the pad and your feet flat on the platform.
Pull the hip pad or lap bar across your hips and adjust it so it sits on the crease of the hips, not on your stomach.
Set your feet so that your shins will be roughly vertical when your hips are at the top, and take hold of the handles.
Drive your hips up by squeezing the glutes until your thighs are level with your torso, and hold briefly at the top.
Lower under control until your hips are just short of the bottom of the range, and repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
cues: Get the pad on the hip crease. Sitting it up on the stomach is the only genuinely uncomfortable thing this machine does, and it is fixed by moving the pad, not by adding padding.
Finish with the hips, not the lower back. If the ribs flare at the top you have run out of hip extension and started arching, which is where the machine stops training the glutes.
This is the hip thrust to reach for when the bench and barbell are taken -- the back pad and platform are part of the frame, so there is no setup to get wrong.
exercises.author: RepDB / Sergei Argutin
exercises.attribution: Exercise data and illustrations by RepDB (https://repdb.co/exercise/plate-loaded-glute-drive/), RepDB Free Tier 1.0 (https://github.com/RepDB/exercise-dataset/blob/main/LICENSE-DATA.md).

exercises.name: Plate-Loaded Lat Pulldown
exercises.instructions: Sit at a plate-loaded (lever) lat pulldown machine with your thighs secured under the pads. Grip the handles overhead with arms fully extended. Pull the handles down toward your upper chest by driving your elbows down and back, squeezing your lats at the bottom. Return slowly to full extension. Resistance comes from weight plates loaded on the machine's lever arms rather than a cable stack.
cues: Keep the torso near vertical; leaning back turns it into a row.
Let the arms extend fully at the top of each rep.
Set the seat so the handles start above your head with arms fully extended.
Drive the elbows down and back rather than pulling with the hands.
exercises.author: trs1800
exercises.attribution: "Plate-Loaded Lat Pulldown" by trs1800 from wger (https://wger.de/en/exercise/2623/view/), CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/). Adapted: formatting simplified.

exercises.name: Plate-Loaded Lateral Raise
aliases: Elevación Lateral en Máquina de Discos
exercises.instructions:
Set the seat height so that the pivot of the arm pads lines up with the point of your shoulders when you sit down.
Load the plate horns evenly on both sides and sit with your back flat against the pad.
Place the outside of your upper arms against the pads with your elbows bent and your arms hanging down.
Push out and up against the pads until your upper arms are roughly level with your shoulders.
Lower under control until your arms are back at your sides, and repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
cues: Set the seat first. If the pivot sits below your shoulder the pads drive your arm across your body instead of out to the side, and the side deltoid stops being the muscle doing the work.
Push with the arm, not the hand. The handles are there to stop your arms sliding off the pads -- gripping hard pulls the biceps and forearms into a raise that should be all deltoid.
Stop at shoulder height. Going higher hands the last part of the rep to the traps, and the machine will happily let you.
exercises.author: RepDB / Sergei Argutin
exercises.attribution: Exercise data and illustrations by RepDB (https://repdb.co/exercise/plate-loaded-lateral-raise/), RepDB Free Tier 1.0 (https://github.com/RepDB/exercise-dataset/blob/main/LICENSE-DATA.md).

exercises.name: Plate-Loaded Seated Dip Machine
aliases: Máquina de Fondos Sentado con Discos
exercises.instructions:
Load the plates evenly on the sleeve and adjust the seat so the handles are at about shoulder height when you are seated.
Sit upright with your back against the pad and grip the handles at your sides with your elbows bent.
Keep your shoulders down and your chest up, then press the handles down by straightening your elbows.
Squeeze your triceps at the bottom, with your arms straight but not locked out hard.
Let the handles rise back up under control until your elbows are bent to about 90 degrees.
Repeat for the planned repetitions, then return the lever to its safety stop before you stand up.
cues: Start light and add plates gradually; if the handles stop short of full extension the load is too heavy.
Keep the elbows close to your sides and your back against the pad so the work stays on the triceps.
Do not let the shoulders roll forward or shrug as the handles rise; stop where the stretch in the chest and shoulders is comfortable.
exercises.author: RepDB / Sergei Argutin
exercises.attribution: Exercise data and illustrations by RepDB (https://repdb.co/exercise/plate-loaded-seated-dip-machine/), RepDB Free Tier 1.0 (https://github.com/RepDB/exercise-dataset/blob/main/LICENSE-DATA.md).

exercises.name: Plate-Loaded Shrug
aliases: Encogimiento de Hombros en Máquina de Discos
exercises.instructions:
Load the plate horns evenly and stand on the machine platform, facing away from the frame.
Take a handle in each hand with your arms hanging straight down at your sides and your shoulders relaxed.
Stand tall with your chest up, your chin level and your knees soft.
Shrug your shoulders straight up toward your ears as high as they will go, and hold for a moment at the top.
Lower under control until your shoulders are fully down, and repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
cues: Shrug straight up. Rolling the shoulders adds travel but no extra trap work, and it takes the shoulder joint through a loaded circle for nothing.
Keep the arms straight and passive. Bending the elbows turns the movement into a short upright row and takes the load off the traps.
The handles hanging at your sides are what this machine is for -- there is no bar to clear your thighs, so you can stand upright and use a full range without shortening the top.
exercises.author: RepDB / Sergei Argutin
exercises.attribution: Exercise data and illustrations by RepDB (https://repdb.co/exercise/plate-loaded-shrug/), RepDB Free Tier 1.0 (https://github.com/RepDB/exercise-dataset/blob/main/LICENSE-DATA.md).

exercises.name: Plow Pose
exercises.instructions:
Lie on your back with the arms alongside the body, palms down.
Lift both legs overhead and support the lower back with the hands.
Lower the toes towards the floor behind the head, keeping the legs as straight as comfort allows.
Hold the position for the prescribed time, breathing steadily and keeping the head still.
Roll down one vertebra at a time with the hands supporting the back.
cues: Never turn the head while you are in the pose; the neck is loaded and must stay neutral.
Rest the toes on a chair or a stack of cushions if the floor is out of reach.
Skip this pose entirely if you have any neck complaints.

exercises.name: Plyo Lunge
exercises.instructions:
Start in a forward lunge with one foot ahead of the other.
Drop into a deep lunge with the back knee almost touching the floor.
Drive both feet off the floor, switching legs in mid-air.
Land softly in a lunge with the opposite leg forward.
Continue alternating without pausing.
cues: Land softly with bent knees to absorb impact.
Switch the leg position fully — do not just hop in place.
Keep the torso upright — do not pitch forward.
exercises.author: RepDB / Sergei Argutin

exercises.name: Plyo Push-Up
exercises.instructions:
Set up in a standard push-up position with hands shoulder-width.
Lower yourself with control until the chest nearly touches the floor.
Drive up explosively so the hands leave the floor.
Land softly with the elbows slightly bent.
Repeat without pausing for the prescribed reps.
cues: Keep the body in a straight line — no piking or sagging.
Land softly with bent elbows to absorb impact.
Drop to knees if you cannot clear the floor cleanly.
exercises.author: RepDB / Sergei Argutin
exercises.attribution: Exercise data and illustrations by RepDB (https://repdb.co/exercise/plyo-push-up/), RepDB Free Tier 1.0 (https://github.com/RepDB/exercise-dataset/blob/main/LICENSE-DATA.md).

exercises.name: Posterior Pelvic Tilt
aliases: Pelvic Tilt Drill / Supine Pelvic Tilt
exercises.instructions: Lie on your back with knees bent, feet flat on the floor. Flatten your lower back against the floor by tilting your pelvis posteriorly, engaging your abs and glutes. Hold 5 seconds, release. This retrains pelvic positioning to counter anterior pelvic tilt.

exercises.name: Posterior Step To Overhead Reach
exercises.instructions:
Stand with your feet hip-width apart and your arms by your sides.
Take a step back with your right foot, landing on the ball of your foot.
Bend your left knee and lower your body into a lunge position.
As you lower into the lunge, simultaneously reach your arms overhead.
Pause for a moment at the bottom of the lunge, then return to the starting position by pushing through your left heel and bringing your right foot forward.
Repeat the movement on the other side, stepping back with your left foot and bending your right knee.
Continue alternating sides for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: Posterior Tibialis Stretch
exercises.instructions:
Sit on the ground with your legs extended in front of you.
Loop the rope around the ball of your foot and hold the ends of the rope with your hands.
Gently pull the rope towards you, flexing your foot and stretching your calf muscles.
Hold the stretch for 20-30 seconds.
Release the tension on the rope and relax your foot.
Repeat the stretch on the other leg.

exercises.name: Potty Squat
exercises.instructions:
Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, toes pointing slightly outward.
Lower your body down by bending your knees and pushing your hips back as if you were sitting on a chair.
Keep your chest up and your back straight throughout the movement.
Lower yourself until your thighs are parallel to the ground or as low as you can comfortably go.
Pause for a moment at the bottom, then push through your heels to return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: Potty Squat With Support
exercises.instructions:
Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, toes pointing slightly outward.
Hold onto a stable support, such as a chair or wall, for balance.
Lower your body down into a squat position by bending your knees and pushing your hips back.
Keep your chest up and your back straight throughout the movement.
Pause for a moment at the bottom, then push through your heels to return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: Power Clean
exercises.instructions:
Start with the barbell on the ground in front of you, with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Bend down and grip the barbell with an overhand grip, slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Keep your back straight and chest up as you lift the barbell off the ground, extending your hips and knees.
As the barbell reaches your mid-thigh, explosively pull it upwards, shrugging your shoulders and pulling your elbows high and to the sides.
As the barbell reaches its highest point, quickly drop underneath it, rotating your elbows around and catching the barbell on your shoulders in a front squat position.
Stand up with the barbell, fully extending your hips and knees.
Lower the barbell back down to the starting position, keeping control of the weight throughout the movement.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: Power Point Plank
exercises.instructions:
Start in a high plank position with your hands directly under your shoulders and your body in a straight line from head to toe.
Engage your core and squeeze your glutes to maintain a stable position.
Lower your body down onto your forearms, one arm at a time, maintaining a straight line from head to toe.
Hold this position for the desired amount of time, keeping your core and glutes engaged.
To return to the starting position, push through your forearms and lift your body back up into a high plank position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: Preacher Curl
exercises.instructions:
Sit at a preacher bench with your upper arms resting on the pad.
Hold an EZ-bar with an underhand grip.
Curl the bar up toward your shoulders.
Lower with control until arms are nearly straight.
Repeat.
cues: Avoid bouncing at the bottom to protect the biceps tendon.
Keep your wrists neutral rather than letting them bend back.
Don't shrug your shoulders as the bar rises.

exercises.name: Preacher Hammer Curl
exercises.instructions:
Sit at a preacher bench with a dumbbell in each hand.
Rest your upper arms on the pad with palms facing each other.
Curl the dumbbells up while keeping your wrists neutral.
Squeeze your biceps at the top of the movement.
Lower the dumbbells with control.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.

Avoid locking out the elbows completely at the bottom.
Control the lowering phase rather than dropping the weight.

Place your hands behind your head with your elbows pointing outwards.
Engaging your abs, slowly lift your upper body off the ground, curling forward until your torso is at a 45-degree angle.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your upper body back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: Prone Twist On Stability Ball

Place your hands behind your head or cross them over your chest.
Engage your core muscles and slowly lift your upper body off the ball, keeping your back straight.
Rotate your torso to one side, bringing your shoulder towards your hip. Keep your hips and legs stable throughout the movement.
Pause for a moment, then return to the starting position.
Repeat the rotation to the other side.
Continue alternating sides for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: Pseudo Planche Push Ups
exercises.instructions:
Start in a push-up position with your hands turned so fingers point back.
Lean your shoulders forward past your wrists.
Lower your chest toward the floor by bending your elbows.
Keep your body in a straight line.
Press back up while maintaining the forward lean.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
cues: The further you lean forward, the harder each rep becomes.
Keep your elbows close to your body as you lower.
Keep your shoulder blades protracted and your body rigid.

exercises.name: Pull-Ups (Neutral Grip)
exercises.instructions:
Execution
• 
Pulling phase (concentric):
• Drive your elbows down and back, pulling your chest toward your hands.
• Keep your shoulders depressed and retracted (avoid shrugging).
• Focus on squeezing your lats and upper back at the top.
• 
Top position:
• Chin should clear or reach the level of your hands.
• Pause briefly and contract your lats hard.

exercises.name: Pull-Ups (Wide Grip)
exercises.instructions:
Execution
• 
Pulling phase (concentric):
• Drive your elbows down and slightly back, pulling your chest toward the bar.
• Focus on leading with your chest, not your chin.
• Keep your shoulders depressed (avoid shrugging).
• 
Top position:
• Chin should clear the bar (or at least reach bar level).
• Pause for a brief squeeze in your lats.

exercises.name: Push-Up
exercises.instructions:
The push-up is a fundamental bodyweight exercise that targets the chest, arms, and shoulders while engaging the core for stability. It requires no equipment and is excellent for building upper body strength.
Instructions:
• Start in a plank position with hands placed slightly wider than shoulder-width, feet together, and body in a straight line from head to heels.
• Engage your core and lower your body by bending your elbows, keeping them close to your body or flared slightly outward.
• Lower until your chest nearly touches the ground while maintaining a neutral spine.
• Push through your palms to return to the starting position, fully extending your arms.

exercises.name: Push-Ups | Decline
exercises.instructions:
Decline push-ups are another modified version of the traditional push-up that target the upper body muscles in a different way. To perform a decline push-up, elevate your feet on an elevated surface, such as a bench, chair, or step, while placing your hands on the ground in a push-up position. Lower your body towards the ground while maintaining a straight line from your shoulders to your ankles, and then push back up to the starting position.
Unlike the inclined push-up, the decline push-up places more emphasis on the shoulders and triceps, while still engaging the chest muscles to a lesser extent. By elevating your feet, you increase the difficulty of the exercise by placing more weight on your upper body, forcing your shoulders and triceps to work harder to push your body back up. The decline push-up can be a great way to challenge your upper body strength and improve your ability to perform other push-up variations. As with any exercise, be sure to use proper form and start with a height that is appropriate for your strength and fitness level.

exercises.attribution: "Push-Ups | Decline" by anon1337 from wger (https://wger.de/en/exercise/1112/view/), CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/). Adapted: formatting simplified.

exercises.name: Push-Ups | Parallettes
exercises.instructions:
Parallettes push-ups are a variation of the traditional push-up that are performed with the hands on parallel bars, known as parallettes. To perform a parallettes push-up, assume a push-up position with your hands on the parallettes and your feet on the ground. Lower your body towards the ground while keeping your elbows close to your sides, and then push back up to the starting position.
Parallettes push-ups place more emphasis on the chest and shoulders compared to traditional push-ups, as they allow for a greater range of motion in the shoulder joint. This increased range of motion can also help to improve shoulder stability and mobility. Additionally, parallettes push-ups engage the core muscles more than traditional push-ups, as the instability of the parallettes requires greater activation of the core muscles to maintain proper form.
The added challenge of balancing on the parallettes also requires greater upper body strength and control, making parallettes push-ups a more advanced variation of the traditional push-up. They can be a great way to challenge yourself and add variety to your upper body workout routine. As always, be sure to use proper form and start with a level that is appropriate for your strength and fitness level.

exercises.name: Quad Sets
exercises.instructions:
What Are Quad Sets?
Quad sets are a fundamental exercise used in knee rehabilitation. They focus on strengthening the quadriceps muscles located at the front of the thigh. This exercise is particularly beneficial for individuals recovering from knee injuries or surgeries.
How to Perform Quad Sets
Steps to Execute Quad Sets
• Positioning: Sit or lie down with your legs straight.
• Tightening: Tighten the quadriceps muscles while keeping the leg straight. You should see the kneecap move upward.
• Holding: Maintain the contraction for about 5 seconds.
• Releasing: Relax the muscle after the hold.
• Repetitions: Aim for 10 to 15 repetitions, gradually increasing as strength improves.
Tips for Effective Quad Sets
• Ensure no other muscles are contracting to assist the quadriceps.
• Perform the exercise on a flat surface, like a bed or couch, with a towel or pillow under your heel for comfort.
• It is recommended to do these exercises multiple times a day, especially during the early stages of recovery.
Benefits of Quad Sets
• Restores Muscle Function: Helps rebuild strength in the quadriceps.
• Improves Stability: Enhances stability in the knee joint.
• Increases Range of Motion: Aids in regaining mobility after injury or surgery.
Incorporating quad sets into your rehabilitation routine can significantly aid in recovery and improve overall knee function.

exercises.name: Rack Pull
exercises.instructions:
Set the safety pins in a power rack at knee height and place a loaded barbell on them.
Stand with feet hip-width apart and grip the bar just outside your legs.
Brace your core, retract your shoulder blades, and drive through your legs to lift the bar.
Lock out your hips and knees fully at the top.
Return the bar to the pins under control and reset before the next rep.
cues: Use a hip-hinge pattern — keep the bar close to your body throughout.

Focus on upper back tightness to prevent rounding at heavy weights.

Hold the resistance band with an underhand grip, palms facing up, and arms extended down by your sides.
Keeping your upper arms stationary, exhale and curl the resistance band up towards your shoulders.
Pause for a moment at the top, squeezing your biceps.
Inhale and slowly lower the resistance band back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: Reverse Lunge
exercises.instructions:
Stand holding dumbbells at your sides.
Step one leg back and lower your knee toward the floor.
Lower until your front thigh is parallel to the floor.
Push through your front heel to return to standing.
Repeat on both sides.
cues: Keep the front knee tracking in line with your toes.
Stay upright through the torso rather than leaning forward.
Lower the back knee softly instead of dropping it to the floor.

exercises.name: Reverse lunges
exercises.instructions:
Starting position:
Stand straight, feet hip-width apart.
Steps:
• Step backward with one leg so it can bend comfortably to a 90 degree angle.
• Slowly bend both knees to form 90 degree angles.
• Return to the starting position.
• Repeat, alternating legs.

exercises.name: Reverse Nordic Curl
exercises.instructions: Natural Leg Extension is alternative to Leg Extension machine with no equipment.
cues: Open your knees shoulder apart
Squeeze the glutes and posterior pelvic tlit
Activate abs and keep the upper body straight.

exercises.name: Reverse Plank
exercises.instructions:
Sit on the floor with your legs extended in front of you.
Place your hands behind you with fingers pointing toward your feet.
Lift your hips off the floor to form a straight line from head to heels.
Squeeze your glutes and brace your core.
Hold the position for the desired duration.
Lower your hips with control to exit.
cues: Don't let your hips sag as the hold progresses.
Keep your gaze up to maintain a neutral neck.
Press evenly through your palms to reduce wrist strain.
exercises.author: RepDB / Sergei Argutin
exercises.attribution: Exercise data and illustrations by RepDB (https://repdb.co/exercise/reverse-plank/), RepDB Free Tier 1.0 (https://github.com/RepDB/exercise-dataset/blob/main/LICENSE-DATA.md).

exercises.name: Reverse Plank Dips
exercises.instructions:
Sit with the legs straight and the hands on the floor behind the hips, fingers pointing forward.
Press into the hands and heels and lift the hips into a straight-leg reverse plank.
Bend the elbows straight back and lower the hips a short way towards the floor.
Push back up until the arms lock out, keeping the hips high.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
cues: Keep the hips lifted at the bottom; sitting down between reps removes the load.
Keep the elbows tracking straight back rather than flaring outwards.
Bend the knees if the straight-leg version is too demanding on the hamstrings.
exercises.author: RepDB / Sergei Argutin
exercises.attribution: Exercise data and illustrations by RepDB (https://repdb.co/exercise/reverse-plank-dips/), RepDB Free Tier 1.0 (https://github.com/RepDB/exercise-dataset/blob/main/LICENSE-DATA.md).

exercises.name: Reverse Plank With Leg Lift
exercises.instructions:
Sit on the ground with your legs extended in front of you and your hands resting on the ground behind you, fingers pointing towards your feet.
Press through your hands and lift your hips off the ground, coming into a reverse plank position.
Engage your core and lift one leg off the ground, extending it straight up towards the ceiling.
Hold for a moment, then lower your leg back down.
Repeat with the other leg.
Continue alternating legs for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: Reverse Snow Angel
exercises.instructions: Lay flat on your stomach with your arms extended in front of you on the ground as your legs are lying flat. Lift both your arms and move them to your side slowly. Then, move them back.

exercises.name: Reverse Tabletop Hip Pulses
aliases: Pulsos de Cadera en Mesa Invertida
exercises.instructions:
Sit with the knees bent, the feet flat and the hands on the floor behind you.
Press into the hands and feet and lift the hips until the trunk is level with the knees.
Keeping the elbows straight, lower the hips a few centimetres.
Squeeze the glutes to lift them back to level.
Pulse for the desired number of repetitions and lower down.
cues: Keep the arms locked: bending the elbows turns this into a dip.
Drive the lift from the heels and the glutes, not from the lower back.
Keep the chest open and the shoulders down away from the ears.
exercises.author: RepDB / Sergei Argutin

exercises.name: Reverse Tabletop Hold
exercises.instructions:
Sit with the knees bent, the feet flat and the hands on the floor behind you, fingers pointing towards the heels.
Press into the hands and feet and lift the hips until the trunk is level with the knees.
Open the chest, draw the shoulders away from the ears and look straight ahead.
Hold the position for the prescribed time with the hips high.
Lower the hips under control to finish.
cues: Push the floor away rather than hanging on the shoulders.
Keep the knees stacked over the ankles and pointing straight ahead.
Let the head follow the line of the spine instead of dropping it back.
exercises.author: RepDB / Sergei Argutin
exercises.attribution: Exercise data and illustrations by RepDB (https://repdb.co/exercise/reverse-tabletop-hold/), RepDB Free Tier 1.0 (https://github.com/RepDB/exercise-dataset/blob/main/LICENSE-DATA.md).

exercises.name: Reverse V-Squat
exercises.instructions:
Step into the V-squat machine facing the pad, the opposite way from the regular V-squat, so that your chest rests against the pad and your shoulders sit under the shoulder pads. Place your feet on the platform about shoulder width apart and release the safety.
Brace your core and lower yourself by bending your knees and pushing the hips back until your thighs are roughly parallel to the platform. Drive back up through the heels without locking out the knees.
Compared to the regular V-squat, the reversed position shifts the emphasis towards the glutes and hamstrings.
exercises.author: aboksz
exercises.attribution: "Reverse V-Squat" by aboksz from wger (https://wger.de/en/exercise/2620/view/), CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/). Adapted: formatting simplified.

exercises.name: Reverse Wood Chops
exercises.instructions:
• Attach a looping resistance band to a rack below knee height
• Grip the other end of the band like holding a baseball bat with both hands
• Stretch the band facing it
• Start with your hands at the side of your hips, knees bent
• Rotate your hips while moving your hands towards over the top of your opposite shoulder
• Imagine the motion as striking a baseball with a bat
cues: Keep arms almost fully extended throughout
Use as much force as possible

exercises.name: Reverse-grip pull-ups
exercises.instructions: Pull-ups on the bar with your thumbs pointing outward.

exercises.name: Revolved Chair Pose
exercises.instructions:
Set up in chair pose with the knees bent, the hips back and the palms together at the chest.
Keep the knees level with each other so the hips do not open into the twist.
Rotate the chest to one side and hook the opposite elbow outside that thigh.
Press the palms together and hold for the prescribed time, lengthening the spine on each inhale.
Come back to centre and repeat on the other side.
cues: Line the knees up before you twist; a knee sliding forward fakes most of the rotation.
Rotate from the mid-back rather than pulling with the arm against the leg.
Keep the weight in the heels so the position stays a squat, not a lean.
exercises.author: RepDB / Sergei Argutin
exercises.attribution: Exercise data and illustrations by RepDB (https://repdb.co/exercise/revolved-chair-pose/), RepDB Free Tier 1.0 (https://github.com/RepDB/exercise-dataset/blob/main/LICENSE-DATA.md).

exercises.name: Revolved Crescent Lunge
exercises.instructions:
Step into a high lunge with the front knee over the ankle and the back heel lifted.
Bring the palms together at the chest and square both hips towards the front of the mat.
Rotate the chest towards the front leg and hook the opposite elbow outside the thigh.
Hold the twist for the prescribed time, pressing the back heel towards the wall behind you.
Unwind and repeat on the other side.
cues: Keep the back leg straight and long; it is what stops the twist collapsing into the hips.
Drop the back knee to the floor for an easier version with the same rotation.
Lengthen the spine first, then rotate — twisting a rounded back gets you nowhere.
exercises.author: RepDB / Sergei Argutin
exercises.attribution: Exercise data and illustrations by RepDB (https://repdb.co/exercise/revolved-crescent-lunge/), RepDB Free Tier 1.0 (https://github.com/RepDB/exercise-dataset/blob/main/LICENSE-DATA.md).

exercises.name: Right levator scapulae stretch
exercises.instructions:
Starting position:
Start standing up or sitting down. Turn your head to the right, around 45 degrees or just above your nipple. Place your left hand behind your back or sit on it. Take your right hand and use it to hold the back of your head. Lean your head down slightly.
Steps:
• After assuming the starting position, press your head against your right hand with slight force. Your hand should press back with equal force, so that your head doesn't move. Hold this position.

exercises.attribution: "Right levator scapulae stretch" from wger (https://wger.de/en/exercise/1014/view/), CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/). Adapted: formatting simplified.

exercises.name: Right neck stretch
exercises.instructions:
Starting position:
Sit or stand with your back straight.
Steps:
• Tilt your head to the side.
• Take the hand closer to your head and use it to grab your head from the other side.
• Push with your hand against your head and with your head against your hand so that the forces balance out and your head stays still.
• Maintain this tension until the end of the exercise.
exercises.author: wger contributors
exercises.attribution: "Right neck stretch" from wger (https://wger.de/en/exercise/1009/view/), CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/). Adapted: formatting simplified.

exercises.name: Ring Dead Hang
exercises.instructions:
Grip a pair of gymnastic rings with a neutral grip, palms facing each other.
Hang with your arms fully extended and feet off the ground.
Let the rings rotate naturally; do not fight the grip.
Keep your shoulders engaged (no shrug to the ears) and core lightly braced.
Hold for the desired duration.
cues: Breathe steadily rather than holding your breath.
Build hold duration gradually as your grip strengthens.
Step down under control before your grip fails completely.
exercises.author: RepDB / Sergei Argutin
exercises.attribution: Exercise data and illustrations by RepDB (https://repdb.co/exercise/ring-dead-hang/), RepDB Free Tier 1.0 (https://github.com/RepDB/exercise-dataset/blob/main/LICENSE-DATA.md).

exercises.name: Ring Dips
exercises.instructions:
Support yourself on the rings with arms locked out.
Lower your body by bending the elbows until upper arms are parallel to the ground.
Press back up to the starting position.
Repeat.
cues: Keep the rings close to your body.
Turn the rings out at the top for additional chest activation.
exercises.author: RepDB / Sergei Argutin
exercises.attribution: Exercise data and illustrations by RepDB (https://repdb.co/exercise/ring-dips/), RepDB Free Tier 1.0 (https://github.com/RepDB/exercise-dataset/blob/main/LICENSE-DATA.md).

exercises.name: Ring Face Pull
exercises.instructions:
Grip the rings and lean back so your body is at an angle.
Pull the rings toward your face, flaring elbows to the sides.
Hold briefly, then return.
Repeat.
cues: Adjust your body angle to control difficulty.
Externally rotate your arms at the top.
exercises.author: RepDB / Sergei Argutin
exercises.attribution: Exercise data and illustrations by RepDB (https://repdb.co/exercise/ring-face-pull/), RepDB Free Tier 1.0 (https://github.com/RepDB/exercise-dataset/blob/main/LICENSE-DATA.md).

exercises.name: Ring L-Sit
exercises.instructions:
Set the rings at about hip height and grip them with the arms straight beside the body.
Press down on the rings and lift the body into the support position, with the shoulders pushed down and away from the ears.
Turn the rings out slightly, brace the abdominals and raise the straight legs until they are parallel to the floor.
Hold the position, keeping the rings steady and the knees locked.
Lower the legs, then the body, under control.
cues: Keep the arms locked and the shoulders pushed down; do not sag between the rings.
Build up from tucked holds, and from parallettes or a dip station, before moving to rings.
Point the toes and squeeze the legs together.
exercises.author: RepDB / Sergei Argutin
exercises.attribution: Exercise data and illustrations by RepDB (https://repdb.co/exercise/ring-l-sit/), RepDB Free Tier 1.0 (https://github.com/RepDB/exercise-dataset/blob/main/LICENSE-DATA.md).

exercises.name: Ring Muscle-Up
exercises.instructions:
Hang from the rings with a false grip, palms facing each other.
Pull explosively, driving the chest up to the rings.
Transition the elbows over the rings as the chest rises.
Press to full arm extension at the top.
Lower under control through the transition back to the hang.
cues: A false grip is essential for the transition.
Drive the elbows down hard during the transition.
Build the strength with negatives and band-assisted reps first.
exercises.author: RepDB / Sergei Argutin
exercises.attribution: Exercise data and illustrations by RepDB (https://repdb.co/exercise/ring-muscle-up/), RepDB Free Tier 1.0 (https://github.com/RepDB/exercise-dataset/blob/main/LICENSE-DATA.md).

exercises.name: Ring Plank
exercises.instructions:
Set the rings at about knee height and take hold of them with the arms straight under the shoulders.
Step the feet back into a plank, with the body in a straight line from head to heels.
Brace the abdominals and glutes and press the rings down and slightly out to keep them steady.
Hold the position without letting the hips sag or the rings drift apart.
Step the feet in and stand up to finish.
cues: Keep the rings close to the sides of the chest; if they swing, place the feet wider.
Push the floor away through the rings so the shoulder blades stay wide.
Raise the rings to make the hold easier and lower them to make it harder.
exercises.author: RepDB / Sergei Argutin
exercises.attribution: Exercise data and illustrations by RepDB (https://repdb.co/exercise/ring-plank/), RepDB Free Tier 1.0 (https://github.com/RepDB/exercise-dataset/blob/main/LICENSE-DATA.md).

exercises.name: Ring Push-Up
exercises.instructions:
Set the rings just above floor height.
Grip the rings and assume a plank position with arms straight.
Lower the chest toward the rings, keeping the elbows close to the body.
Press back up to full arm extension.
Repeat for the prescribed reps.
cues: Keep the rings turned out at the top to engage the chest.
Brace the core — the rings will magnify any wobble.
Drop to knees to scale the difficulty.
exercises.author: RepDB / Sergei Argutin
exercises.attribution: Exercise data and illustrations by RepDB (https://repdb.co/exercise/ring-push-up/), RepDB Free Tier 1.0 (https://github.com/RepDB/exercise-dataset/blob/main/LICENSE-DATA.md).

exercises.name: Ring Row
exercises.instructions:
Set the rings at hip to chest height.
Grip the rings with palms facing each other, lean back at an angle with arms straight.
Brace the core and pull the chest toward the rings.
Squeeze the shoulder blades together at the top.
Lower under control to a full-arm extension.
cues: The lower the body angle, the harder the row.
Keep the body in a straight line — do not let the hips sag.
Pull the elbows back, not flared out, for more lat involvement.
exercises.author: RepDB / Sergei Argutin
exercises.attribution: Exercise data and illustrations by RepDB (https://repdb.co/exercise/ring-row/), RepDB Free Tier 1.0 (https://github.com/RepDB/exercise-dataset/blob/main/LICENSE-DATA.md).

exercises.name: Ring Support Hold
exercises.instructions: Hold yourself in a support position on gymnastic rings with arms straight at sides. Focus on keeping rings turned out slightly and maintaining hollow body position. This is an isometric hold for chest, shoulders, and triceps.
exercises.author: wger contributors
exercises.attribution: "Ring Support Hold" from wger (https://wger.de/en/exercise/1832/view/), CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/). Adapted: formatting simplified.

exercises.name: Rings Inverted Row
exercises.instructions:
Set the rings just above hip height.
Lie under the rings and grip them with palms facing each other.
Walk the feet forward so the body forms a straight line.
Pull the chest toward the rings, squeezing the shoulder blades.
Lower under control to a full-arm extension.
cues: Keep the body in a straight line — heels through head.
Squeeze the glutes and core to prevent sagging.
Elevate the feet on a box for a harder version.
exercises.author: RepDB / Sergei Argutin

exercises.name: Rocking Frog Stretch
exercises.instructions:
Start by kneeling on the ground with your knees hip-width apart.
Place your hands on the ground in front of you for support.
Slowly lean forward, shifting your weight onto your hands and extending your legs behind you.
Keep your back straight and engage your glutes as you push your hips back and up towards the ceiling.
Hold this position for a few seconds, feeling a stretch in your glutes.
Slowly return to the starting position by bending your knees and lowering your hips back down.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: Rocking Triceps Pushdown
exercises.instructions: Set your feet below the rope and lean your upper body towards the rope. Set one foot back. Push down the rope and lean your entire body back onto the rear foot as you push down to get your hands behind your body. Don't forget to bring your chest to the front during the pushdown. As you release the rope slowly, lean your body back onto the front foot.
cues: Don't use your body weight to pull the rope down. Let the triceps do all the work.
The back&forth movement of your body is purely to keep a more perpendicular position between arm and rope.

exercises.name: Rocky Pull-up Pulldown
exercises.instructions:
Stand in front of a pull-up bar with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Reach up and grab the bar with an overhand grip, slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Hang from the bar with your arms fully extended and your body straight.
Engage your back muscles and pull your body up towards the bar, leading with your chest.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your body back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: Roll Down

exercises.name: Roller Back Stretch

exercises.name: Roller Body Saw

exercises.name: Roller Hip Lat Stretch

Place your hands on the roller for support.
Slowly roll the roller forward, extending your hips and stretching your glutes.
Hold the stretch for a few seconds, then roll back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: Roller Hip Stretch
exercises.instructions:
Start by sitting on the ground with your legs extended in front of you.
Place the roller under your glutes, just above your knees.
Lean back and place your hands on the ground behind you for support.
Engage your glutes and slowly roll the roller forward, bending your knees and bringing them towards your chest.
Pause for a moment at the end of the movement, feeling a stretch in your glutes.
Slowly roll the roller back to the starting position, extending your legs.

exercises.name: Roller Reverse Crunch
exercises.instructions:
Lie flat on your back with your arms extended straight above your head and your legs straight out in front of you.
Place the roller between your feet and grip it with your toes.
Engaging your abs, lift your legs off the ground and curl your knees towards your chest, rolling the roller towards your body.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your legs back down to the starting position, rolling the roller away from your body.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: Roller Seated Shoulder Flexor Depresor Retractor
exercises.instructions:
Sit on a flat surface with your legs extended in front of you.
Hold the roller with both hands, palms facing down, and place it on your thighs.
Lean forward slightly and roll the roller away from your body, extending your arms straight in front of you.
Pause for a moment, then slowly roll the roller back towards your body, bending your arms and bringing the roller back to your thighs.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: Roller Seated Single Leg Shoulder Flexor Depresor Retractor
exercises.instructions:
Sit on a flat surface with your legs extended in front of you.
Hold the roller with both hands, palms facing down, and place it on your thighs.
Lean back slightly and engage your core muscles.
Raise the roller up to shoulder level, keeping your arms straight.
Slowly lower the roller back down to your thighs.

exercises.name: Rope Climb
exercises.instructions:
Grip the rope as high as you can with both hands.
Either wrap the rope around one foot (S-hook or J-hook) or pinch it between both feet.
Pull with your arms and bring your knees up, then clamp the rope with your feet and stand up on the foot lock.
Reach higher with one hand, then the other, release the feet, and clamp the rope again higher up.
Repeat until you reach the top of the rope.
Descend hand-under-hand with the feet controlling the speed — never slide.
cues: Learn the foot lock before attempting longer climbs; it doubles your work capacity.
Never drop from the top; controlled descent is part of the exercise.

exercises.name: Row
exercises.instructions: In strength training, rowing (or a row, usually preceded by a qualifying adjective — for instance a seated row) is an exercise where the purpose is to strengthen the muscles that draw the rower's arms toward the body (latissimus dorsi) as well as those that retract the scapulae (trapezius and rhomboids) and those that support the spine (erector spinae). When done on a rowing machine, rowing also exercises muscles that extend and support the legs (quadriceps and thigh muscles). In all cases, the abdominal and lower back muscles must be used in order to support the body and prevent back injury.

exercises.name: Running
exercises.instructions:
Start from an easy jog and build into your pace over the first few minutes rather than setting off at target speed.
Land with your foot under your hips, not out in front, and keep the contact with the ground short and quiet.
Run tall through the hips with a slight forward lean from the ankles, not a fold at the waist.
Bend your elbows to about ninety degrees and drive your arms forward and back, keeping them off your chest.
Breathe rhythmically and keep your shoulders, jaw and hands loose.
Hold the pace for the desired time or distance, then jog and walk for a few minutes to finish.
cues: Build weekly distance gradually. Almost every running injury comes from adding volume faster than the tendons and bones adapt, not from a single hard run.
Most of your running should be easy enough to talk in. Running every session at a middling hard pace is the fastest way to plateau.
Shorten your stride and let your cadence rise if you feel yourself thudding — reaching for a longer stride puts the brakes on with every footfall.

Only move your torso during the exercise. Reduce weight if necessary.

exercises.name: Scorpion Kick
exercises.instructions:
Get into the push-up position with your shoulders directly above your hands and your feet hip-width apart.
Make sure that your body forms a straight line from your head to your heels.
Now pull your right knee towards your chest. While keeping your knee bent, lift your right leg as high as possible with your lower right leg pointing straight up.
Now rotate your hips so that your right foot swings over your left leg.
Continue to rotate and move your right foot towards the floor until you are forced to roll onto the outside of your left standing foot. Make sure that you do not rotate your upper body.
Now return to the starting position and repeat the exercise with your left leg.

exercises.name: Seated Band Row
exercises.instructions: Sit on the floor with your legs straight out in front of you and your back tall. Loop a resistance band around the soles of both feet and hold one end in each hand, arms extended and a slight bend in the knees. Pull the band toward your lower ribs by driving your elbows straight back and squeezing your shoulder blades together. Keep your chest up and your torso still rather than rocking backward to move the band. Extend the arms slowly to return. Because the torso stays upright and supported, this is a useful row when a bent-over position is uncomfortable, and it needs no anchor point.
cues: Keep the torso still; don't rock backward to finish the rep.
Shorten your grip on the band for more resistance.
Sit tall: hips stacked under the shoulders, chest up.
Pull to the lower ribs, not the chest.

exercises.name: Seated Corkscrew
exercises.instructions:
To
do this abs and obliques exercise, start with your hands back behind your body
and bring your knees in and across, really trying to contract the obliques.
Then extend your legs back out to starting position and repeat toward the
opposite side of the abs.
Beginners

challenging reverse crunches variation. That’s ok because it gives you a
place to start and something to improve upon.

exercises.name: Seated Dip Machine

Keep your shoulders down and your chest up, then press the handles down by straightening your elbows.
Squeeze your triceps at the bottom, with your arms straight but not locked out hard.
Let the handles rise back up under control until your elbows are bent to about 90 degrees.
Repeat for the planned repetitions, keeping your back against the pad.
cues: Keep the elbows close to your sides so the work stays on the triceps.
Do not let the shoulders roll forward or shrug as the handles rise; stop where the stretch in the chest and shoulders is comfortable.
Keep your back against the pad; leaning forward shifts the work toward the chest.

exercises.name: Seated hip abduction (machine)
exercises.instructions:
Starting Position:
• Adjust the seat height so that your knees are aligned with the pivot point of the machine.
• Sit with your back flat against the backrest, maintaining good posture.
• Place the outside of your thighs against the machine's padded levers.
• Position your feet flat on the footrests or platform of the machine.
• Grasp the handles or sides of the seat for stability.
• Ensure your spine is neutral and your core is slightly engaged.
Movement:
• Exhale as you slowly push your legs outward against the resistance pads.
• Focus on initiating the movement from your hips, not your knees.
• Continue opening your legs until you feel a strong contraction in your outer hips and thighs.
• Hold the fully abducted position briefly (1-2 seconds) to maximize muscle engagement.
• Inhale as you slowly control the return of your legs to the starting position, resisting the weight throughout the movement.
• Avoid allowing the weight stack to touch down between repetitions to maintain constant tension on the muscles.
• Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, maintaining control throughout the set.

exercises.name: Seated Knee Extension with Overpressure
exercises.instructions: A gentle stretch to restore full knee extension. Sit with one leg stretched out in front of you and the heel propped on the floor or a low surface, so the knee is unsupported. Place both hands on the thigh just above the kneecap. Keeping the leg relaxed, gently press down through the hands toward the floor until you feel a stretch behind the knee, and hold for about three seconds before releasing. The pressure should produce a stretch, never sharp pain. Repeat for the prescribed number of repetitions, then switch legs.
cues: Hold about three seconds, then release fully before the next rep.
Often prescribed after knee surgery or injury to restore full extension.
Keep the heel propped and the leg relaxed; the hands do the work.
Press gently toward a stretch, never into sharp pain.

exercises.name: Shinbox IR Stretch
exercises.instructions:
• Starting Position: Sit on the floor with both hips and knees bent at 90-degree angles.
• Leg Placement:
Place one leg in front of you (external rotation) and the other leg out
to the side/behind you (internal rotation). The shins and knees should
remain flat on the ground.
• The Movement:
Keeping your hips square, hinge your torso forward or tilt it laterally
(side-to-side) toward the front leg to deepen the stretch.
• Target Areas:
Stretches the glutes and piriformis (front leg) and the hip flexors and
quads (back leg). Engages the core and obliques during lateral flexion.
• Goal: Improves hip mobility, specifically internal and external rotation, and relieves lower back tension.

exercises.name: Shoulder Shrug
exercises.instructions: The shoulder shrug (usually called simply the shrug) is an exercise in weight training used to develop the upper trapezius muscle. The lifter stands erect, hands about shoulder width apart, and raises the shoulders as high as possible, and then lowers them, while not bending the elbows, or moving the body at all. The lifter may not have as large a range of motion as in a normal shrug done for active flexibility. It is usually considered good form if the slope of the shoulders is horizontal in the elevated position.

exercises.name: Shoulder Tap
exercises.instructions:
Start in a high plank position with your hands directly under your shoulders and your body in a straight line.
Engage your core and lift your right hand off the ground, reaching across to tap your left shoulder.
Place your right hand back on the ground and repeat with your left hand tapping your right shoulder.
Continue alternating shoulder taps while keeping your hips and torso stable.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: Shoulder Tap Push-up
exercises.instructions:
Start in a high plank position with your hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart and your body in a straight line from head to heels.
Lower your body towards the ground by bending your elbows, keeping them close to your sides.
As you push back up, lift your right hand off the ground and tap your left shoulder.
Return your right hand to the ground and repeat the push-up, this time lifting your left hand and tapping your right shoulder.
Continue alternating shoulder taps with each push-up repetition.
Maintain a stable core and avoid excessive hip rotation throughout the exercise.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: Shoulder width three-point push-up
exercises.instructions: Get into a push-up position with your shoulders directly above your hands and your feet hip-width apart. Draw your belly button in towards your spine and tighten your abdominal muscles. Lift your left foot about five centimetres off the floor. Point your toes straight down. Do not move your hips. Your body forms a straight line from your head to your heels throughout the exercise. Now bend your elbows, lower your chest to the floor and push yourself back up. Repeat the exercise on the other side.

Prop yourself up on your forearm, keeping your elbow directly below your shoulder.
Engage your core and lift your hips off the ground, creating a straight line from your head to your feet.
While keeping your core engaged, lift your top leg as high as possible without rotating your hips.
Pause for a moment at the top, then lower your leg back down.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch sides.

exercises.name: Side Lunge
exercises.instructions:
Stand with feet hip-width apart and hands at your chest.
Step one leg wide to the side, keeping the other leg straight.
Bend the stepping knee and push your hips back into a lateral squat.
Keep your chest up and the working heel planted.
Drive through the bent leg to return to standing.
Complete reps on one side, then switch.
cues: Push your hips back as you bend the stepping knee.
Keep your trailing leg straight and both heels planted.
Keep your chest up rather than rounding forward.

exercises.name: Side Lying Floor Stretch
exercises.instructions:
Lie on your side with your legs straight and your bottom arm extended straight overhead.
Bend your top knee and place your foot on the ground in front of your bottom leg.
Reach your top arm over your head and grab onto something stable, like a wall or a piece of furniture.
Slowly lift your bottom leg off the ground, keeping it straight, until you feel a stretch in your side.
Hold the stretch for 20-30 seconds, then slowly lower your leg back down.
Repeat on the other side.

Support your head with your bottom arm.
Lift the bottom leg upward toward the ceiling.
Lower the leg back down under control.
Complete reps on one side, then switch.
cues: Keep your hips stacked vertically to avoid rolling backward.
Keep the movement slow and deliberate through the short range of motion.
Pause briefly at the top of each lift.

exercises.name: Side Plank Leg Lift Hold
aliases: Plancha Lateral con Elevación de Pierna Isométrica
exercises.instructions:
Set up in a side plank on the forearm with the elbow under the shoulder and the feet stacked.
Lift the hips until the body forms a straight line from the ankles to the head.
Raise the top leg to roughly hip height, keeping the toes pointing forward.
Hold the position for the prescribed time, keeping the hips high and the supporting shoulder stacked over the elbow.
Lower the leg and the hips under control and repeat on the other side.
cues: Push the supporting shoulder away from the ear so the chest does not collapse towards the floor.
Stop the set when the hips start to drop, not when the leg gets tired.
Bend the bottom knee to the floor for an easier version that keeps the leg lift intact.

Lower the leg back down with control without dropping the hips.
Complete reps on one side, then switch.

Lead the leg lift with the heel, not the toes.
Keep the body in one straight line from head to bottom foot.

Hold the stretch for 15-30 seconds.
Repeat on the other side, tilting your head to the left and applying pressure with your left hand.
Repeat the stretch 2-3 times on each side.

exercises.name: Side-Lying Hip Abduction Hold
aliases: Abducción de Cadera Acostado de Lado Isométrica
exercises.instructions:
Lie on one side with the legs stacked and straight, and support the head on the lower arm.
Brace the trunk so the torso stays square and does not roll backwards.
Lift the top leg to about 30 to 45 degrees, keeping the toes pointing forward.
Hold the leg there for the prescribed time, breathing normally.
Lower the leg under control and repeat on the other side.

Take the leg slightly behind the line of the body to bias the glute medius.
Rest the top hand on the floor in front of you if balance is the limiting factor.

exercises.instructions:
Lie on one side with the bottom leg straight and the top leg crossed over it, foot flat on the floor.
Support the head on the lower arm and keep the hips stacked vertically.
Lift the bottom leg as high as it will go with the knee straight and the toes pointing forward.
Hold that lifted position for the prescribed time without rolling the hips back.
Lower the leg under control and repeat on the other side.
cues: The range is short; a few centimetres of lift with a still pelvis beats a big swing.
Keep the lifted leg in line with the torso rather than drifting forward.
Press the top foot lightly into the floor if you need to steady the position.

exercises.name: Side-Lying Lateral Raise
exercises.instructions:
Lie on your side on a flat bench with your bottom arm supporting your head or gripping the bench edge.
Hold a dumbbell in your top hand with your arm resting along your side.
Keeping your elbow slightly bent, raise the dumbbell upward until your arm is perpendicular to the floor.
Pause briefly at the top, then lower the dumbbell slowly back to your side.
Complete all reps on one side before switching.
cues: Keep your torso still — only the working arm should move.
The lying position removes momentum and isolates the lateral deltoid effectively.
Use a lighter weight than your standing lateral raise — the leverage is more challenging.

exercises.name: Side-to-side Chin
exercises.instructions:
Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and your knees slightly bent.
Grasp a pull-up bar with an overhand grip, hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Hang from the bar with your arms fully extended and your body relaxed.
Pull yourself up by bending your elbows and bringing your chin towards the bar, while keeping your body straight.
Once your chin is above the bar, lower yourself back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: Side-to-side Toe Touch (male
exercises.instructions:
Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and your arms extended to the sides.
Bend at the waist to the right, reaching your right hand towards your right foot while keeping your left hand extended to the side.
Return to the starting position and then bend at the waist to the left, reaching your left hand towards your left foot while keeping your right hand extended to the side.
Repeat the side-to-side bending motion for the desired number of repetitions.

exercises.name: Single Arm Dumbbell Bench Press
aliases: Press de Banca con Mancuerna a Un Brazo
exercises.instructions:
Lie back on a flat bench with the feet planted on the floor and a dumbbell held at chest level in one hand.
Rest the free hand on your stomach or hold it out to the side for balance.
Press the dumbbell up over the chest until the arm is straight.
Pause briefly at the top without letting the body roll toward the pressing arm.
Lower the dumbbell slowly to the side of the chest.
Complete the repetitions on one side, then switch arms.
cues: Squeeze the glutes and keep the shoulder blades pinned to the bench to resist rotation.
Lower to the side of the chest, with the elbow about 45 degrees from the body.
Use a weight you can hold level without twisting; add load only when both sides match.

exercises.name: Single Arm Push-up
exercises.instructions:
Start in a push-up position with your hands shoulder-width apart and one hand placed slightly wider than the other.
Engage your core and lower your body towards the ground by bending your elbows, keeping your back straight.
As you lower yourself, shift your weight to one side and lift the opposite arm off the ground, extending it straight out to the side.
Push through your chest and triceps to raise your body back up to the starting position, while simultaneously lowering your extended arm back to the ground.
Repeat the movement, alternating the arm you extend with each repetition.

exercises.name: Single Arm Tricep Pushdown
aliases: Extensión de Tríceps a Un Brazo en Polea
exercises.instructions:
Attach a single handle to a high cable pulley.
Grasp the handle with one hand and keep your elbow pinned to your side.
Press the handle down until your arm is fully extended.
Squeeze the triceps at the bottom.
Slowly return to the start position.
Complete reps on one side, then switch.
cues: Keep your elbow pinned to your side throughout.
Avoid leaning forward to add momentum.
Fully extend your arm at the bottom for a complete contraction.

exercises.name: Single Dumbbell Svend Press
exercises.instructions:
Stand tall and hold a single dumbbell upright in front of your sternum, the handle running vertically between your flat palms.
Squeeze your palms hard into the dumbbell so the chest takes the tension and the weight cannot slip.
Press the dumbbell straight forward until your arms are almost straight, keeping it at chest height the whole way out.
Pause briefly without letting the squeeze go, then draw the dumbbell back to your chest under control.
Repeat for the recommended number of repetitions.
cues: The squeeze on the dumbbell is what makes the exercise. If you are gripping the handle instead of crushing the weight between flat palms, the chest is not working.
Use a light dumbbell. Your palms hold it up on friction alone, so the grip sets the ceiling long before the chest does.
Keep the elbows slightly bent at the lockout and the dumbbell at sternum height throughout; letting it sag toward the hips takes the pecs out of it.

exercises.name: Single Leg Bridge With Outstretched Leg
exercises.instructions:
Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet flat on the ground.
Extend one leg straight out in front of you.
Engage your glutes and lift your hips off the ground, forming a straight line from your knees to your shoulders.
Hold for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your hips back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch legs.

exercises.name: Single Leg Calf Raise

Hold a wall or rail for balance with one hand.
Drop the heel below platform level for a deep stretch.
Drive up onto the toes as high as possible.
Lower under control. Complete reps per side, then switch.

Use a slow eccentric for full stretch.
Hold a dumbbell on the working side once bodyweight is too easy.

exercises.name: Single Leg Calf Raise (on A Dumbbell
exercises.instructions:
Stand with your feet hip-width apart and hold a dumbbell in one hand.
Lift one foot off the ground and balance on the other foot.
Slowly raise your heel as high as possible, using your calf muscles.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower your heel back down.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch to the other leg.

exercises.name: Single Leg Extension

Rest the other foot on the floor or let it hang.
Extend the working leg until it is nearly straight.
Squeeze the quadriceps at the top.
Lower the leg back down under control.
Complete reps on one side, then switch.

Lower the weight under control rather than letting it drop.
Keep your back flat against the pad.

exercises.name: Single Leg Lying Leg Curl
aliases: Curl de Pierna Tumbado a Una Pierna

Lie face down on a lying leg curl machine.
Position one ankle under the pad, keeping the other foot off the machine.
Curl the working leg by bringing your heel toward your glute.
Squeeze the hamstring at the top.
Lower the leg back down under control.
Complete reps on one side, then switch.

Avoid jerking the pad up with momentum.
Start with the weaker leg and match its reps on the other side.

exercises.instructions: Strength training exercise where you push a weight away from your body using one leg at a time on a leg press machine. exercises.name: Single Leg RDL
exercises.instructions:

• Brace your core and lift one leg off the ground.
• Keep your back straight, hinge at the hips while lowering your torso forward, ensuring you don’t rotate your hips.
• Lower until you feel a stretch in your standing leg's hamstring, then return to standing position. Repeat on both sides.
cues: Maintain balance and focus on proper form to prevent injury.

exercises.name: Single Leg RDL Hold
aliases: Peso Muerto Rumano a Una Pierna Isométrico
exercises.instructions:
Stand on one leg with a slight bend in the knee and the arms hanging in front of you.
Hinge at the hip, sending the free leg straight back as the torso tips forward.
Keep the back flat and the hips square to the floor.
Stop when the torso and the free leg are roughly parallel to the floor and hold the position.
Return to standing under control, then switch legs.
cues: Think of a seesaw: the torso and the free leg move together.
Keep the hips level; do not let the free hip rotate upward.
Fix your gaze on a point on the floor ahead to help your balance.

exercises.name: Single Leg Romanian Deadlift
aliases: Peso Muerto Rumano a Una Pierna
exercises.instructions:
Stand on one leg holding a dumbbell in each hand in front of your thighs.
Keep a slight bend in the standing knee.
Hinge at the hip while extending the free leg behind you.
Lower the dumbbells along your standing leg until you feel a hamstring stretch.
Drive through the heel to return to upright.
Complete reps on one side, then switch.
cues: Keep your hips square to the floor as you hinge.
Fix your eyes on a spot ahead to help balance.
Reach the rear heel straight back rather than letting the leg swing wide.

exercises.name: Single Leg Squat (pistol) Male
exercises.instructions:
Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and arms extended in front of you.
Lift your right foot off the ground and extend it forward.
Slowly lower your body down by bending your left knee and pushing your hips back.
Keep your chest up and your back straight as you lower yourself down.
Lower until your left thigh is parallel to the ground, or as low as you can comfortably go.
Pause for a moment at the bottom, then push through your left heel to return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch legs.

exercises.name: Single-arm cable pushdown
exercises.instructions:
Single-arm cable pushdown is a unilateral isolation exercise that targets the triceps brachii. By working one arm at a time, it helps correct strength imbalances between sides while also engaging the core for stability.
Starting position:
Stand facing the cable machine with your feet shoulder-width apart. Attach a single handle to the high pulley. Grab the handle with one hand using an overhand grip (pronated), with your elbow bent at approximately 90° and tucked close to your body. Keep your core braced and your back straight.
Execution:
Push the handle downward in a controlled motion by extending your elbow until your arm is fully extended. Hold the contraction for 1 second at the bottom, then slowly return to the starting position.
cues: Keep your elbow fixed and close to your body throughout the movement
Do not swing your torso or use momentum
Control the return — do not let the weight pull your arm up
Keep your wrist neutral and firm

exercises.attribution: "Single-arm cable pushdown" by evtimovgeorg from wger (https://wger.de/en/exercise/1969/view/), CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/). Adapted: formatting simplified.

Rotate the upper torso to get into the starting position and bend the upper torso a little bit sidewise.
Place the unused hand on the knee.
Pull the cable while rotating the upper torso.

exercises.name: Single-Arm Chest-Supported Dumbbell Row
aliases: Remo con Mancuerna a Una Mano con Pecho Apoyado

Lie face-down on an incline bench holding a dumbbell in one hand, arm hanging straight down.
Row the dumbbell up to your side, driving your elbow past your torso.
Squeeze your shoulder blade at the top, then lower under control.
Complete all reps on one side before switching arms.
cues: Working one side at a time lets you focus on a full contraction without the other arm compensating.
Keep your chest pressed into the bench throughout to avoid using momentum.
Match the rep count on both sides to avoid imbalances.

exercises.name: Single-Arm Dumbbell Overhead Tricep Extension
aliases: Extensión de Tríceps sobre la Cabeza con Mancuerna a Un Brazo
exercises.instructions:
Stand or sit holding a dumbbell in one hand overhead, arm fully extended.
The palm faces forward; the other hand can hold your waist or an upright for stability.
Bend the elbow to lower the dumbbell behind the head in a controlled arc.
Keep the upper arm vertical and close to the head throughout.
Extend the elbow to return the dumbbell overhead.
Complete all reps on one side, then switch.
cues: Only the forearm moves — the upper arm stays glued in place.
Don't let the torso lean to the side; this is also a core exercise.

exercises.name: Single-Arm Dumbbell Row
aliases: Remo con Mancuerna a Un Brazo

Place one knee and hand on a bench for support.
Hold a dumbbell in the other hand with arm extended.
Pull the dumbbell up toward your hip, squeezing your shoulder blade.
Lower the dumbbell with control.
Repeat on both sides.
cues: Avoid rotating the torso to hoist the weight higher.
Let your arm extend fully at the bottom for a complete stretch.
Keep your back flat from head to hips throughout the set.

exercises.name: Single-arm dumbbell shoulder press
exercises.instructions: Press the dumbbell vertically overhead in a controlled motion until your arm is fully extended, without locking the elbow. Slowly lower the dumbbell back to the starting position at shoulder height.
cues: Keep your core tight throughout the movement to avoid lateral trunk lean
Do not arch your lower back as you press
Keep your wrist neutral and aligned with your forearm
Control the descent — do not drop the weight

exercises.name: Single-Arm Hammer Curl
exercises.instructions:
Stand with your feet about hip-width apart and hold one dumbbell at your side with the palm facing inward.
Brace your trunk and keep the working upper arm beside your ribs as the arm hangs straight.
Curl the dumbbell toward your shoulder without rotating the palm or swinging the torso.
Squeeze the elbow flexors at the top, then lower the dumbbell under control until the arm is straight.
Complete the repetitions on one side, then switch arms and repeat.
cues: Let the weaker arm set the repetitions and weight so both sides receive the same work.
Keep the wrist neutral and the shoulder quiet; the movement should come from bending the elbow.
Use a controlled lowering phase instead of dropping the dumbbell from the top.

exercises.name: Single-Arm Lat Pulldown
exercises.instructions: Sit at the lat pulldown machine and grab the single handle with a neutral grip. Keep your torso stable, your chest lifted, and your shoulder blades slightly retracted. Start with your arm fully extended overhead, then pull the handle down toward your upper chest following a controlled, slightly diagonal path. Focus on engaging the latissimus dorsi while keeping the shoulder depressed and avoiding any torso rotation. Slowly return to the starting position, maintaining full control throughout the movement.
cues: Keep the shoulder down and away from the ear during the entire movement.
Avoid leaning or twisting your torso to assist the pull.
Control the eccentric phase and avoid letting the weight pull you upward.
Focus on pulling with the back muscles, not with the biceps.
Keep the elbow close to the body in the final part of the pull.

exercises.name: Single-Arm Machine Shoulder Press
aliases: Press de hombros unilateral en máquina
exercises.instructions:
Adjust the seat so the working handle starts around shoulder height and sit with your back firmly against the pad.
Grip one handle with the wrist straight and keep the free hand on the support or resting comfortably.
Press the handle upward without leaning away from the back pad or rotating the torso.
Lower the handle under control until the elbow is just below the starting line, then repeat.
Complete the repetitions on one side, adjust the seat if needed, and train the other side.
cues: Start with the weaker arm and let it set the weight and repetitions for both sides.
Keep the ribs down and the back against the pad instead of leaning away from the working arm.
Stop short of a painful shoulder position; the machine path should feel controlled from bottom to top.
exercises.author: RepDB / Sergei Argutin
exercises.attribution: Exercise data and illustrations by RepDB (https://repdb.co/exercise/single-arm-machine-shoulder-press/), RepDB Free Tier 1.0 (https://github.com/RepDB/exercise-dataset/blob/main/LICENSE-DATA.md).

exercises.name: Single-Arm Plate-Loaded Lateral Raise
aliases: Elevación Lateral a Un Brazo en Máquina de Discos
exercises.instructions:
Set the seat height so the pad pivot lines up with your shoulder, and load only the side you are about to work.
Sit with your back flat against the pad and place the outside of your working upper arm against its pad.
Hold the handle on the free side or rest that hand in your lap, and keep your torso square to the seat.
Push the working arm out and up against the pad until the upper arm is level with your shoulder, then lower it under control.
Complete all the repetitions on that side, then load and work the other side.
cues: Match the sides on the weaker arm, not the stronger one. Working one side at a time only tells you about an imbalance if you let the weaker side set the number.
Do not let the torso tip toward the working side. With load on one arm only, the machine no longer balances itself and leaning turns the raise into a side bend.
Start with the weaker arm so it sets the target, and give both sides the same rest.

exercises.name: Single-Leg Balance with Eyes Closed
exercises.instructions: A balance and proprioception drill. Stand on one leg with the knee slightly bent and the other foot lifted clear of the floor, then close your eyes and hold the position. Without visual feedback the ankle and hip stabilisers have to do the work, so expect noticeable wobble. Stand within reach of a wall, counter or chair so you can steady yourself if needed. Hold for the prescribed time, then switch legs. Commonly prescribed in rehabilitation after ankle or knee injury.
cues: Keep the standing knee soft, not locked.
Let the foot and ankle work; small wobbles are the point.
Stand near a wall or counter so you can catch yourself.

Keep the hips level and the torso upright; the shifting weight of the bell constantly changes your centre of mass, which is what trains the hip and ankle stabilisers. Complete the prescribed number of circles, reverse direction, then switch legs. Use a light bell to start.
cues: Move the bell smoothly, passing hand to hand behind the back.
